# dsh-doc-anchor
**Turn PDF / HTML / LaTeX / Markdown documents into locatable evidence surfaces for DeepSeek Harness
urn PDF / HTML / LaTeX / Markdown documents into locatable evidence surfaces for DeepSeek Harness.**
*No reader, no renderer, no translation — just coordinates, immutable snapshots, and an evidence rec
ord anyone can re-check.*
English · 简体中文
## What it does
`dsh-doc-anchor` is the **PDF/HTML/LaTeX → evidence** step of the research plugin family. It answers
one question: *where exactly in this document does that text live?*

- Two immutable snapshots per document: the **original bytes** and the **extracted text**.
- Locator
s into the extracted text: **page ranges** (PDF), **sections** (headings), **tables**, **paragraphs*

*, plus exact char offsets.
- A **REP v1 evidence record** (`@perrylink/dsh-research-core`) so `clai
m-check`, `cite-verify`, `statcheck` and `research-report` can cite the document without trusting a

summary.
- Optional helpers: `doc_locate` (find a verbatim quote), `doc_tables` (read table grids ba

ary.
- Optional helpers: `doc_locate` (find a verbatim quote), `doc_tables` (read table grids back).
## What it does not do
- **No OCR.** A scanned PDF fails with an explicit `parse_failed`; v0.1 never guesses text from pixe

ls.
- **No PDF table reconstruction.** `doc_tables` says so instead of inventing a grid.
- **No rend
ering, reading, translating or summarising.** Extracted text is the raw text layer, normalized only

in whitespace.
- **No document execution.** `<script>`/`<style>` are dropped, LaTeX macros are never

expanded, `\input` files are not followed.
- **No archives.** DOCX/ODT/EPUB/ZIP are rejected by nam
e — nothing is unpacked, so zip bombs have no surface.
## Compatibility
| DeepSeek Harness | **`dsh-v0.2.1-rc.5`** (verified 2026-11-08); peer line `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0 \|\| >
errylink/dsh-research-core ^0.1.0` (shared protocol), `@deepseek-ai/cordis ^4.0.5-alpha.1`, `@deepse

ek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ^3.18.5-alpha.1` |
| Runtime dependencies | **zero** |
The REP core package is a **required peer** (it is the shared protocol, not a sibling feature plugin

When `ctx.researchEvidence` is mounted, evidence goes into that store; otherwise the plugin creates
its own `EvidenceStore` under `root`, so it also works alone.
## Tools
### `doc_anchor`
Takes `path` **or** `content`.
| Parameter | Type | Notes |
| `path` | string | workspace-relative or absolute; must stay inside `workspaceRoot` (traversal + sy

mlink escapes rejected) |
| `content` | string | inline document text (mutually exclusive with `path

`) |
| `name` | string | file name for media-type detection with inline content |
| `mediaType` | en

um | `application/pdf` · `text/html` · `text/x-latex` · `text/markdown` · `text/plain` |
| `title` |

string | evidence title (defaults to the file name) |
| `persist` | boolean | `false` = dry run, no

snapshots and no record |
| `maxAnchors` | integer | per-call cap (hard cap 500, REP v1) |
Returns `{ ok, evidenceId, snapshotId, textSnapshotId, mediaType, pages, chars, anchorCount, truncat
ed, anchors[], tableCount, warnings[], injectionSuspected, recordPath }`.
**Anchors index into `textSnapshotId`.** `kind` is `page` (with `page`), `section` (with `label: h1.
.h6`), `table` (with `value: t.N`), or `paragraph` (with `value: para.N`); every anchor carries `cha
th `value: t.N`), or `paragraph` (with `value: para.N`); every anchor carries `charStart`/`charEnd`.
### `doc_locate`
`{ query, evidenceId?, textSnapshotId?, maxResults?, ignoreCase? }` → `{ ok, count, hits[{charStart,

charEnd, quote, page?}] }`.
Exact match against the extracted text; `evidenceId` also maps hits to
PDF pages. Zero hits is a normal answer.
### `doc_tables`
`{ evidenceId, maxRows? }` or `{ path, maxRows? }` → `{ ok, count, tables[{index, source, header?, r

ows, rowsTruncated, charStart, charEnd}], warnings[] }`.
HTML `<table>` and LaTeX `tabular` are pars
ed structurally; PDF tables report empty with a warning.
### Error codes
`INVALID_INPUT` · `NOT_FOUND` · `NOT_A_FILE` · `PATH_ESCAPE` · `TOO_LARGE` · `PAGE_LIMIT` · `UNSUPPO
RTED_TYPE` · `PARSE_FAILED` · `EMPTY_DOCUMENT` · `STORE_ERROR` · `EVIDENCE_UNKNOWN`
[该节后续省略]
## Security boundaries
- **Path safety**: `path` is resolved against the workspace, then `realpath`-checked; `..`, absolute

paths outside, and symlinks pointing outside are rejected with `PATH_ESCAPE`.
- **Size/time**: byte
, page and character caps are enforced before/while parsing; over-limit input fails instead of being

truncated.
- **Untrusted content**: documents are data. Scripts/styles/iframes are dropped, LaTeX i
s never expanded, and instruction-like text raises `prompt_injection_suspected` (bounded, metadata-o

nly warning) without changing behaviour.
- **No network**: the plugin never fetches a URL. Remote ca

pture belongs to `dsh-cite-verify` / `dsh-research-report`.
- **No execution**: no PDF JavaScript, n
o macros, no external references, no archive extraction.
## Known limitations (v0.1)
- **Scanned PDFs** have no text layer → `PARSE_FAILED`. OCR is planned as an optional external backe

nd, never bundled.
- **CID fonts without `ToUnicode`** render as replacement characters; a warning i

s emitted per page.
- **PDF tables** are not reconstructed.
- **HTML** is tag-scanned, not a full HT

ML5 parser; malformed markup degrades gracefully but may lose nested structure.
- **LaTeX** is a str
uctural scanner: `\input` is not followed, custom macros are not expanded, and only common text comm

ands are flattened.
- **`.docx` / archives** are rejected by design.
